AUTHOR: Zhang
TITLE: Unsupervised Underwater Fish Detection Fusing Flow and Objectiveness
VENUE: 2016 IEEE WINTER APPLICATIONS OF COMPUTER VISION WORKSHOPS (WACVW)
DATA: Own/partner NOAA luminance-only underwater fish videos
V_EV: Sec. 4.1: 'We have used optical flow to detect fish in the hazy underwater environment in which objects about 10 meters away are obscured.'
D2: Training samples from first 20 min of one sequence; test on video from a different camera
D_EV: Sec. 5: '100,000 samples were generated from the first 20 minutes of video. Fish detection was tested from a different camera monitoring the same area.'
R_EV: Sec. 5: 'Fish detection was tested from a different camera monitoring the same area.' (same NOAA data/area; no other dataset)
C_EV: Sec. 5: 'Detection scores are displayed in 7(d). A simple threshold removes negative scores.'
E_EV: Sec. 5: 'AP of the Selective Search only = 56%, and AP of the fused proposal (green curve) = 66%.' (detection metrics only)
ARCH: CaffeNet (AlexNet) R-CNN style binary classifier with Selective Search + optical-flow proposals and modified NMS
NOTE: Platform/environment not described (NOAA stock-assessment videos). Test video from 'a different camera monitoring the same area' coded as video-level split, not external (P2: same campaign; camera system not stated as different). Score threshold implicitly 0 ('removes negative scores'); MNMS handles overlapping boxes, not duplicate counts, so C5=없음. 'Hazy... 10 meters' coded as qualitative visibility of own data.
AUTHORS_FULL: Zhang, D; Kopanas, G; Desai, C; Chai, S; Piacentino, M
